gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open prices the whole under-$100 8K Hall effect field at each maker's own US store on one date, and none lists a Gamakay board or ChatGPT's own top pick (MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro); read 2026-11-21, the wired Gamakay NS68 ($36.79) sits $0.61 under the Ace 60 Pro ($37.40) and $5.70 under the Epomaker HE68 Lite ($42.49), and three of ChatGPT's shown prices differ from the maker's store by $10 or more.
standout_why: Compared against gamepadsquire.com (cited in chat 2), setupinsider.com and mechanicalkeyboard.net, all opened 2026-11-21. Together they price the HE68 Lite, Redragon K673 HE / K617 HE / K686 HE / K707 HE, AULA F75 HE, Attack Shark R85 HE, MCHOSE Ace 68 V2, RK C84 HE, DAREU EK60 HE and the FUN60 Ultra TMR. None lists the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro, Epomaker HE80, Yunzii RT75 Pro or any Gamakay board, and none gives a dated maker-store price for the full set. Rivals do have part of it: gamepadsquire already gives the HE68 Lite's 128K scan rate and says the FUN60 Ultra TMR keeps 8K on 2.4 GHz. Three pages could not be compared: keebforce.com (cited; certificate error), and pcgamer.com and rtings.com (both cited; only navigation rendered, no article body). The score assumes they do not carry this table.
decides: On price alone the pick is a near-tie in a sub-$45 wired cluster: Gamakay NS68 wired $36.79, MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro $37.40, Redragon K617 HE $39.99, Gamakay NS68 tri-mode $39.99, MCHOSE Ace 68 $41.65, Epomaker HE68 Lite $42.49. That puts the NS68 in the top three on price, and the near-tie rule favours it as the board we can link, provided another angle confirms its 8K rating per connection mode; I could not open Gamakay's pages (HTTP 429). Where each loses: the Ace 60 Pro and FUN60 Ultra are 60% boards with no arrow keys or F-row. The FUN60 Ultra's $59.99 is the bottom of a $59.99–$89.99 range covering wired and tri-mode, and MonsGeek's page showed 'Unavailable' with a waitlist form when read. The HE68 Lite costs $5.70 more than the wired NS68. The HE80 has the lowest scan rate (32,000) and coarsest trigger step (0.02 mm) of the Epomaker boards read. The K673 HE adjusts actuation only in 0.1 mm steps and is cable-only. Yunzii's own page rates the RT75 Pro at 1 ms wireless against 0.1 ms wired, and it is $79.99 at Yunzii, not the $69.99 ChatGPT showed. Among 75% boards the Gamakay NS75 at $63.99 is $16.00 under the RT75 Pro at Yunzii's store, but its 16K scan rate (maker rating, from the brief) is below the HE68 Lite's 128K. The TK75HE V2 ($79.19) and TK75 TMR ($89.99) fit the budget but cost more than double the cheapest boards.
